value.hook: Before reviewing Unix-socket deletion, lsof pathname handling, or a process-fd census
value.title: Socket absence needs a complete holder proof

sections.name: body
sections.value:
#298/#299: a refused Unix connect can be a live Darwin listener with a full backlog. Compare file identity, not /tmp versus /private/tmp text; decode lsof names exactly. Never silently drop an unstat-able bound path: a removed directory alias or renamed directory can leave its listener alive.

A native Linux counterexample used ordinary shared-table pthreads: main called pthread_exit, /proc/<pid>/fd became empty, and a worker still served after the old sweep deleted its socket. A separate controlled handoff replay transferred the fd to an already-scanned process before its source exited. Neither needs PID reuse. #299's final Linux reader therefore returns Unknown, with BLOCKED/exit 2; do not casually restore a census. The macOS lsof walk/SCM_RIGHTS residual remains documented.

For regression proof, remove the young-file brake in owned scratch, assert removed=0 and that the live worker still answers, then force Known-empty: it must delete and fail the safety assertion. Keep native-worker proof distinct from historical/fake-proc replay. Native checks can use a cached, network-disabled container through shared-build; nice the container workload too, not only its host client.

Evidence anchors: R1 verdict 8b358cf; final verdict e63b39ab. Read alongside, not instead of, the existing concurrency-oracle note.
